title: Adaptive Post-Processing Drives Instance-Level Detection in Stroke Lesion Segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2608.16377v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Instance-level lesion detection has been an increasingly larger focal point in medical image segmentation besides the more standard voxel-level overlap. Still, most pipelines are trained and post-processed for voxel overlap alone. In particular, the mismatch is most pronounced for small lesions, where a near-miss prediction---substantial overlap that falls just short of the instance-matching threshold---scores the same as a complete miss. In our ISLES'26 submission, we found that closing this gap mattered far more in post-processing than in architecture design. Our Volume-Conditioned Adaptive Post-Processing (VCAP) scheme adjusts component-size thresholds to each case's predicted lesion burden, improving Lesion-F1 by 0.032 (unbiased cross-fold estimate)---approximately 6 times larger than any architectural change we tested. translated_title: 自适应后处理推动卒中病灶分割中的实例级检测
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.16377v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：实例级病灶检测在医学图像分割中日益成为关注焦点，除了更标准的体素级重叠指标外。然而，大多数流水线仅针对体素重叠进行训练和后处理。特别是，这种不匹配在小病灶中最为明显，其中接近命中的预测——即实质重叠但略低于实例匹配阈值——与完全未命中得分相同。在我们的ISLES'26提交中，我们发现缩小这一差距在后处理中远比在架构设计中重要。我们的体积条件自适应后处理（VCAP）方案根据每个病例的预测病灶负担调整组件大小阈值，将Lesion-F1提高了0.032（无偏交叉折叠估计）——大约是我们测试的任何架构更改效果的6倍。一种为小病灶分割设计的分辨率感知注意力架构（Viola2Plus）展示了这一差距的原因。
tldr: 本文提出体积条件自适应后处理（VCAP）方案，通过根据病例预测病灶负担调整组件大小阈值，显著提升卒中病灶分割的实例级检测性能，其效果远超架构设计改进。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a Volume-Conditioned Adaptive Post-Processing (VCAP) scheme that adjusts component-size thresholds based on predicted lesion burden, substantially improving instance-level detection in stroke lesion segmentation, with gains far exceeding architectural changes.
